rows.question: Do we have official per-game player data for props?
rows.known: Yes. nfl.com/players/<slug>/stats/logs/ publishes a full per-game log per player, and the logs sum exactly to the published season totals (IC-15/16, 5 of 6 players check out).
rows.unknown: Complete coverage of every player, and any per-game data for defensive players.
rows.answer: Props are NOT blocked. Three earlier sessions recorded them as blocked; that was wrong (flag F-01).

rows.question: Does the NFL publish a depth chart with 1st/2nd/3rd string?
rows.known: No. The team depth-chart URL returns 404 for every club tried; the official roster page lists players, jersey numbers, positions and roster status (ACT) but no depth rank.
rows.unknown: Who is the backup at each position. This is not published by the league at all.
rows.answer: Starter-vs-backup replacement cannot be derived from official sources.
rows.unlock: A licensed depth-chart or snap-count feed (see S-02).

rows.question: What do we know about injuries right now?
rows.known: The official Week 10 injury report covers 14 games with practice status and game status per player, and it still shows pre-game records for the Week 10 clubs.
rows.unknown: Severity, expected games missed, and who replaces whom.
rows.answer: We can quantify unavailability by club and position; we cannot say who the backup is.

rows.question: Do we have a 2026 market price to compare our lines against?
rows.known: No. The NFL publishes no prices and this repository holds no licensed 2026 line archive.
rows.unknown: Every closing price, every prop price, every parlay price.
rows.answer: No 2026 edge, divergence or return can be computed or claimed.
rows.unlock: A licensed historical and live odds feed.

rows.question: Is the third-party archive good enough for the backtest?
rows.known: 7,548 regular-season games, 1999-2026, with closing spread and total. Peer sessions spot-checked 45 of 45 official scores with zero mismatches.
rows.unknown: Its licence status, and whether its closing lines are true closing prices.
rows.answer: Usable for research; not usable for any commercial claim.

rows.question: How big must the sample be before a strategy can be believed?
rows.known: L3 computes it: about 2,300 graded decisions for a 55% edge at 80% power.
rows.unknown: Whether any genuine edge exists at all in public data.
rows.answer: The 300-decision gate G1 is a floor, not a sufficient sample.

rows.question: Can luck be removed entirely?
rows.known: No. It can only be bounded: pre-registration, holdout, clustered intervals, placebo tests, FDR control and prospective replication.
rows.unknown: The true edge of any strategy until prospective replication exists.
rows.answer: G12 (prospective replication) is the only gate that genuinely removes hindsight.
rows.unlock: Run the leaderboard forward with timestamped predictions.

rows.question: Which correlations did we actually measure?
rows.known: Team-level: favourite-cover vs over phi = -0.0079; home win vs over phi = +0.0110; home margin vs total and rest vs margin, computed on the holdout.
rows.unknown: Player-level correlations beyond the seven official logs read here.
rows.answer: Team-level pairs are near zero, so multiplicative parlay pricing is defensible for those pairs. Player-level values come from small samples and are labelled as such.
rows.unlock: More official game logs (one page per player per season).

rows.question: What is the injury-to-performance link, quantified?
rows.known: Nothing yet. We have Week 10 availability and the archive's results, but the archive has no injury field.
rows.unknown: Any measured effect of a missing starter or backup on spread or total.
rows.answer: No injury effect is claimed anywhere on this site.
rows.unlock: Historical injury reports joined game by game (see S-05).

rows.question: Does the own-line model beat the closing line?
rows.known: No. In the holdout the own spread is worse than the closing line on mean absolute error.
rows.unknown: Whether a better model with injuries and player data could close the gap.
rows.answer: Own lines are not yet a price. They are a structured projection.
rows.unlock: Add the injury and player features, then re-register the gates.

rows.question: Are the leaderboard rewards real?
rows.known: No. Rewards are competition points, not money, and no strategy has earned any.
rows.unknown: Whether any strategy will ever pass every gate.
rows.answer: Zero points awarded in this release, and that is the honest output.
rows.unlock: Prospective replication with live, timestamped decisions.

rows.question: Are parlays additive or does correlation matter?
rows.known: Measured phi for the pairs we can check; same-player prop combos are positively correlated by construction and their joint hit rate is measured here.
rows.unknown: Book repricing behaviour on correlated combos, which needs real prices.
rows.answer: Correlated legs must be priced jointly, not multiplied. Our own numbers show the gap.

rows.question: Is any team-level signal stable into Week 11?
rows.known: Ratings are shrunk by 6 games and use only official 2026 results.
rows.unknown: Whether mid-season ratings persist; we have one season of official data.
rows.answer: Projections are published with their inputs so the shrinkage is auditable.
rows.unlock: Multiple official seasons with the same pipeline.

rows.question: What is missing to originate player-prop lines with confidence?
rows.known: Seven official per-game logs, read here, plus 75 season leaders.
rows.unknown: Every other player's game log (each needs its own page read), and any prop price.
rows.answer: We can originate props for 7 players today, honestly labelled as small-sample.

rows.question: Which irregularity in the current repo blocks us?
rows.known: Rebuilding the root dashboard silently deletes peer NFL navigation (R-01); the Week 10 injury page still shows pre-game records; the published AVG column does not reproduce yds/att on 4 of 32 rows (IC-07).
rows.unknown: Whether the peer sessions intend to consolidate the eleven NFL namespaces.
rows.answer: None of these blocks publication; all are published on the Flagged page.
rows.unlock: Peer sessions act on R-01 and the consolidation decision.
